video_title: Cousins Live from the NBA Finals with Threads

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on his first playoff experience with the Raptors
quotes.excerpt: I was getting ready for my first playoff appearance in franchise history with the Toronto Raptors.
quotes.quote: I was getting ready for my third season in the NBA with the Toronto Raptors and also I was getting ready for my first playoff appearance in franchise history with the Toronto Raptors. We faced the New York Knicks where we manhandled them in the regular season and that's when I realized the playoffs were a different story because we got in the playoffs and they beat our ass, they swept us 3-0.

quotes.speaker: Robert Horry
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Horry on the 1999 Spurs championship run
quotes.excerpt: I was getting beat by the San Antonio Spurs last game in the Forum, so they shut it down.
quotes.quote: I was getting beat by the San Antonio Spurs last game in the Forum, so they shut it down and then the next year we went to Crypto, well now back then it was Staples, but yeah we got beat by the San Antonio Spurs and they went on and won the NBA championship that year so I remember.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on his career with the Raptors and Knicks
quotes.excerpt: T-Mac was the hall that made it to the Hall of Fame. Tracy was the guy that...
quotes.quote: T-Mac was the hall that made it to the Hall of Fame. Tracy was the guy that, on the back end of his career, playing with the Knicks and the San Antonio, the guy that he just wasn't very good. So for me, I like both organizations actually. I love seeing New York in the finals because I love their fandom. Their fans are crazy, obnoxious, but I love everything about it.

quotes.speaker: Robert Horry
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Horry's prediction for the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: I played in the West my whole career, so I got to roll with the West, so I got to go with the Spurs.
quotes.quote: I played in the West my whole career, so I got to roll with the West, so I got to go with the Spurs. You got to think about the Spurs culture. And the one thing about the Spurs culture, they always do what's right. They going to do what the coach says, they going to toe the line, and more importantly, they going to play with a little nastiness. And so that's what you love about the Spurs. Not saying the Knicks don't do that, I don't know anything about that organization, but I do know about the Spurs organization and once they get to the finals, they very, very rarely lose in the finals.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on Mitchell Robinson's injury
quotes.excerpt: It is a broken pinky, but he also had damage to the fifth metacarpal as well.
quotes.quote: It is a broken pinky, but he also had damage to the fifth metacarpal as well. And so that's basically hand, pinky, you know, but it is the pinky, it is a player that doesn't necessarily need to have the ball in his hands. We saw him today at practice, he had a soft glove on. Yeah, basically he had wrapping on as well as a splint. He's going to have that if not a little bit more when he actually tries to play.

quotes.speaker: Robert Horry
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Horry on playing through injuries
quotes.excerpt: Players know their bodies better than the trainers and doctor staff and when you come to a hand, you can still play.
quotes.quote: Players know their bodies better than the trainers and doctor staff and when you come to a hand, you can still play. But when it comes to a calf and Achilles and you know, if I'm Halliburton, I'm calling my first call is to KD, yo man, tell me what happened, you how did this happen? And then I'm like, nah, because now you look at what happened to him last season with him being out, they got awful. And so he's just too important to the team and to the system. I know it's the finals and everybody's like, what's the finals? I can get, no, you just, I know you gave us a top pick in the draft, but your health and your future is more important than just, you know, the finals.

quotes.speaker: Robert Horry
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Horry on the origin of his nickname
quotes.excerpt: I was with the Houston Rockets in 1995, we played the Spurs and I was zero for eight or zero for nine in the game.
quotes.quote: I was with the Houston Rockets in 1995, we played the Spurs and I was zero for eight or zero for nine in the game and David Robinson went to go double team Dream, because you know that's the series where Dream kind of just killed David Robinson. I pump faked the ball to say I'm selling the corner and took a step in and knocked down one, I made one shot and Craig Kilborn came on the TV and says, oh Big Shot Bob and that's how the name was born right there.

quotes.speaker: Robert Horry
quotes.excerpt: I think Jaden McDaniels because you look at the way, you know, everybody wanted him to get benched and the coach stuck by him.
quotes.quote: I think Jaden McDaniels because you look at the way, you know, everybody wanted him to get benched and the coach stuck by him and so for me, I look at the way he plays defense and I love watching players who play with a joy. Like him and Josh Hart, they play with a joy, they always smiling, they playing hard. So I just think Jaden McDaniels and plus he wears number 25.

quotes.speaker: Malik Rose
quotes.summary_phrase: Malik Rose on the Spurs culture
quotes.excerpt: I think everything, and even ice, if you want to go back to you know, ABA, NBA, you can I throw ice in there.
quotes.quote: I think everything, and even ice, if you want to go back to you know, ABA, NBA, you can I throw ice in there. Got a ton of love and respect for George Gervin, but I think for all of us, you know, these five championship Spurs or whatever, it started with David, you know, the humility, the character, the work ethic, with everything being about winning, not worrying about off the court stuff. We were all blessed to come in under that, that umbrella and Tim was like that, but I would say David helped sharpen that in him.

quotes.speaker: Malik Rose
quotes.summary_phrase: Malik Rose on the Spurs' winning culture
quotes.excerpt: It's about winning games and championships, not selling tickets and filling people in seats and marketing and promotion.
quotes.quote: It's about winning games and championships, not selling tickets and filling people in seats and marketing and promotion and the the the best players on these teams are are allowing their teammates to to to shine and that's how you win. Like no, no one does it by themselves. Long gone are the days of one player winning a championship.

quotes.speaker: Malik Rose
quotes.summary_phrase: Malik Rose's prediction for the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: The Spurs are going to win, but the four there's going to be, I don't know, seven games.
quotes.quote: The Spurs are going to win, but the four there's going to be, I don't know, seven games. Seven games, let's call it seven. I love all my people in New York, so I'm going to give them three games, but it's going to be a point differential of seven points. Whatever it is, it's going to be a very, very close series.

quotes.speaker: James Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: James Jones on the intensity of the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: You know the games have to be played, so when we walked in and they told us like, you know, the AC unit issues.
quotes.quote: You know the games have to be played, so when we walked in and they told us like, you know, the AC unit issues and the game was going to, it was going to be hot, we weren't going to our locker rooms are going to be hot, we're going to have to use fans, you know, you basically just have to figure it out. It's like playing a hot summer gym in Florida in the summer, but you know the NBA finals is is that event, so the date's not moving, the games not being changed, you just have to strap up and and it was a heck of a game, a great series, they just got the best of us, but a memorable time.

quotes.speaker: James Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: James Jones on the importance of depth in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: You have to set the table for your stars because you know going into the series they're not trying to take the role players away.
quotes.quote: You have to set the table for your stars because you know going into the series they're not trying to take the role players away. They're going to try to take away the best players and you're going to have a moment and every role player on the team is going to have a moment and you have to deliver. These these games, these series are usually one player away. Like I look at this the Spurs game seven and Luke Cornett runs down and blocks a shot in transition. That's the play of the of the series, not just the play of the game, that's the play of the series and every player will have that. So as a as a role player, you have to be ready for it and you have to know it's going to come and the team and the players that do it the best, that team is going to win because it's a it's a it's a marathon in the finals.

quotes.speaker: James Jones
quotes.summary_phrase: James Jones on the X-factors for the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: I think Devin Vassell is underrated. He is. His versatility and the things that he brings to that team.
quotes.quote: I think Devin Vassell is underrated. He is. His versatility and the things that he brings to that team, defensively, offensively, like I said, energy, he never never stops, he plays the entire game, a shooter that moves but also a defender that's tough and and then for the Knicks, it's going to be Michael Bridges because at the end of the day, there's going it's going to be who can get stops and and I think when you look at the the the Spurs perimeter with Dylan and with Stefan and and then more importantly, Fox, you got to have someone that can get a stop and I think it's going to be big for Michael.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the Knicks' championship odds and Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: It would be Jalen Brunson if they were to win.

text_blocks.speaker: Cousins
text_blocks.text: Danny Green, who is your MVP?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: It would be Jalen Brunson if they were to win. But I think San Antonio has grown a lot and they have a good chance at also winning in six.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the importance of role players in the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: I think that's what it comes down to.

text_blocks.speaker: Cousins
text_blocks.text: How important are the role players going to be in this series on both sides?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: I think that's what it comes down to. Is Shamet going to have another great series like that? Is Mitchell Robinson or Deuce McBride? I don't know. To upkeep that is tough to do. My banking is that those guys will be more consistent because of what I've seen. The Spurs side, they showed up in Game 7, but Keldon Johnson, Champagnie, Vassell, they had moments, but I don't know if they can do it consistently through a seven-game series.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on why the Knicks are a bad matchup for the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: I think it's a bad matchup for the Spurs, even though they've grown.

text_blocks.speaker: Cousins
text_blocks.text: Do you think Jalen Brunson can handle that?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: The reason I also picked the Knicks is because I think it's a bad matchup for the Spurs, even though they've grown. I seen that cup game and Jalen Brunson was not affected by it. And I think the biggest reason why is because he has more weapons around him. Mitchell Robinson on the glass, those two bigs, it affects him a lot. Rebounding-wise, his activity, it fatigues him. And going through that seven-game series, that's a lot mentally.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the mental preparation for an NBA Finals series
quotes.excerpt: Every player has their routines. I'm going to get tape, I'm going to get stretched, I'm going to lift.
quotes.quote: Every player has their routines. I'm going to get tape, I'm going to get stretched, I'm going to lift after or listen to music. But when you get to the film watch, that's where I think it gets different. You get to hone in on one team. And this, for both teams, there's days in between games. Now, if you lose, you got two or three days for it to linger, but also your body can get some rest. But you're only focusing on film, walkthroughs, every day these opponents, breaking into groups. The bigs go to the bigs, guards, now it's different because it's positionless. But you got to know everybody across the board. This guy, we're going to strong and weak. This guy, we're going to drop. This guy, we're sending left or we're going to shift off him. We're going to close short. We're going to double on him. You have days to prepare.
